description: Redesign app/portfolio/[slug]/page.tsx with structured section header parsing, sticky right sidebar (desktop >=1024px), and improved layout. Add required CSS classes to app/globals.css. FEAT-002 depends on FEAT-001 completing first (content format is set there).
steps: Step 1: Add new CSS classes to the BOTTOM of app/globals.css (after the last existing rule). The classes needed are listed below in 'css_to_add'.

Step 2: Replace the full content of app/portfolio/[slug]/page.tsx with the new layout described below. Keep all existing imports. Add one new import: import type { Project } from '../../data/projects';
Step 3: The layout is a two-column grid on desktop (>=1024px): main content column (left, ~65% width) and sticky sidebar (right, ~35% width). On mobile it is single column with sidebar below content.

Step 4: The content column order is: (a) Hero image full width, (b) Title + category/tags, (c) Author + Role row with Live and GitHub buttons, (d) Client/Inspiration row (only if project.client exists), (e) Parsed content sections, (f) ScreenshotGallery component, (g) Footer author card + all tags, (h) Prev/Next navigation.

Step 5: Content parsing logic: split project.content on double newlines ('\n\n'). For each segment, check if it starts with one of these exact strings: 'The Problem', 'How It Works', 'Tech Stack', 'What I Would Improve'. If it matches, render it as a section header block (hr divider + h3). Otherwise render it as a

tag. No other markdown parsing is needed.

Step 6: The sticky sidebar (desktop only, hidden on mobile) contains three sub-sections: (a) Author card with avatar, name, tagline 'Fullstack Engineer · AI & Web3', (b) Tags list (all project.tags), (c) Related projects: find 2 projects from same category (project.category === other.category) excluding current project. If fewer than 2 found, fill with random other projects. Show each as a mini card with logo, name, excerpt snippet (first 60 chars), and a Link to /portfolio/[id].
Step 7: The Back to All Works nav link stays at the top of the page (above the two-column grid), full width.
Step 8: Prev/Next navigation goes below the main content column (spanning full width or just content column — inside the main column, after the footer section).
Step 9: Run npm run build from /Users/wayphantomme/Documents/wayan-phantom to verify. Fix any TypeScript errors before marking complete.
acceptance_criteria: On desktop (>=1024px), a sticky sidebar is visible on the right with Author, Tags, and Related Projects sections
On mobile (<1024px), the sidebar is hidden and layout is single column
Content paragraphs starting with 'The Problem', 'How It Works', 'Tech Stack', 'What I Would Improve' render as h3 section headers with an hr divider above them
Hero image appears above the title (full width within content column)
Live and GitHub buttons are in the author/role row
Client/Inspiration row only renders when project.client exists
Related projects sidebar section shows 2 projects from same category or random fallback
ScreenshotGallery is still used for the mockups gallery
Prev/Next navigation still works and links to correct adjacent projects
npm run build passes with zero TypeScript errors
verification: Run: npm run build from /Users/wayphantomme/Documents/wayan-phantom — must exit 0 with zero errors
findings: Iteration 1 verification (2025-01): Two-column layout with sticky sidebar implemented and verified. npm run build exits 0 with zero TypeScript errors. All 19 static pages generated. page.tsx uses SECTION_HEADERS = ['The Problem', 'How It Works', 'Tech Stack', 'What I Would Improve'] to detect section headers via para.startsWith(h). CSS classes (post-detail-grid, post-detail-main, post-detail-sidebar, post-sidebar-card, post-section-divider, post-section-header, post-detail-wrap, etc.) appended to globals.css. Sidebar hidden on mobile, sticky on >=1024px. Related projects by category with fallback. ScreenshotGallery, prev/next navigation, client row, author card all working. page_tsx_full:
See implementation note below — write the full file per the layout spec above. Key points: (1) Keep all existing imports (projects, notFound, Link, Metadata, ScreenshotGallery). (2) Keep generateStaticParams and generateMetadata unchanged. (3) Keep AUTHOR constant unchanged. (4) The outer wrapper uses 'post-page' + 'post-detail-wrap'. (5) The section header parsing: const SECTION_HEADERS = ['The Problem', 'How It Works', 'Tech Stack', 'What I Would Improve']; then map paragraphs: if SECTION_HEADERS.some(h => para.startsWith(h)) render <>

{para}

. (6) Related projects: const related = projects.filter(p => p.id !== project.id && p.category === project.category).slice(0, 2); if (related.length < 2) fill with projects.filter(p => p.id !== project.id && !related.includes(p)).slice(0, 2 - related.length). (7) The hero image uses class 'post-blog-hero' (existing). (8) The two-column grid uses 'post-detail-grid'. (9) Left column uses 'post-detail-main'. (10) Right sidebar uses 'post-detail-sidebar'. (11) 'post-detail-wrap' replaces 'post-wrap-blog' as the outer container.
